events.title: Kotlin announced
events.summary: JetBrains announced Project Kotlin on July 19, 2011 — a pragmatic JVM language designed to interoperate with Java.
events.about: Kotlin is JetBrains' modern JVM language — null safety, data classes, coroutines, and 100% Java interop. Google made it the preferred Android language in 2017; it also compiles to JavaScript and native via Kotlin Multiplatform. Teams adopt it to write safer Android and backend code without leaving the Java ecosystem.

narrative.whyChosen: Kotlin became Android's recommended language and a mainstream Java alternative on the JVM.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed a language could be more concise and null-safe than Java while calling existing Java libraries unchanged.
narrative.problemSolved: JetBrains needed a JVM language that compiled as fast as Java and fixed pain points Scala's complexity introduced.
